submitted.rationale: Index 16 (Sb 0.66, the ZnSb2O6 trirutile composition) had the highest measured EQE, 9.8e-4 %. The other two measurements were lower: index 0 gave 3.6e-5 % and index 23 gave -3.2e-4 %. All EQEs are very small under 2.1 eV light, which fits these wide-gap Zn antimonates. The peak response therefore sits in the middle of the composition line.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 3.6e-5 %. This is the Zn7Sb2O12 region; MEGNet's 1.95 eV gap estimate did not translate into photoresponse.
Measured EQE was negative. The small MEGNet gap for Sb-rich ZnSb4O8 did not give any photoresponse.
GP pick. Not measured because my extrapolation toward the Sb-rich end chose index 23 instead.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet-HSE puts ZnSb2O6 trirutile (mp-3188) at 1.97 eV, which is just below the 2.1 eV photon energy. Index 16 (Sb 0.66) sits at the ZnSb2O6 stoichiometry. ZnSb2O4 (4.2 eV) would not absorb. Caveat: MEGNet likely underestimates the gap; experimentally ZnSb2O6 is about 3.4 eV.

Support. MACE puts Zn7Sb2O12 at 0.012 eV/atom above the hull, so it is essentially stable. Index 0 matches its stoichiometry (Sb 0.22), and the XRD at index 0 shows extra peaks not seen at other compositions. Its MEGNet gap of 1.95 eV is below 2.1 eV. Index 16 gave near-zero EQE, so the opposite end of the line is worth testing.

Support. MEGNet gives the Sb-rich ZnSb4O8 phase (Sb 0.8) a small gap of 0.48 eV, so it should absorb 2.1 eV light. EQE rose about 27-fold from index 0 (Sb 0.22) to index 16 (Sb 0.66). At index 23 (Sb 0.82), the 1.904 peak linked to the Sb-rich phase is at its strongest. I'm extrapolating toward the Sb-rich end rather than taking the GP's pick of index 20.
